snippet: Into that tight market, China added indium and its derivatives — including InP — to its export control list on February 4, 2025, requiring government permits for each overseas shipment. China controls roughly 70% of global raw indium output, so the move reaches upstream into the raw material as well as the finished substrate. The result has been opaque, timing-volatile shipment delays. Prices reflect the squeeze: optical-grade two-inch substrates roughly doubled from around $800 per wafer in early 2025, and high-end six-inch wafers climbed more than 250%, against a supply-demand gap estimated to exceed 70%.
